implementation_notes: A record is a transparent carrier for immutable data: components become private final fields with accessors, the class is implicitly final and no setter is generated, so the classic recipe collapses into a declaration. The compiler inserts no defensive copies, so the remaining work is the compact constructor - List.copyOf, Map.copyOf or an array clone for every mutable component. Records cannot extend another class and cannot declare extra instance fields, so the hand-written final class is still the right form when the type must join a hierarchy or keep internal state.
pitfalls: Records are shallowly immutable: without List.copyOf in the compact constructor the record stores the caller's mutable list and the caller's later add() shows up through items().
Collections.unmodifiableList is a view, not a copy: while another holder can still mutate the underlying list, the immutable object appears to change; List.copyOf takes a snapshot instead.
Sharing a mutable element between two records breaks value equality and hashing for both; the elements of an immutable collection must themselves be immutable.

variants.name: final class with private final fields and withers
variants.idiom_name: final class, private final fields, no setters, withers
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-records recipe, still required for Java 8 targets and for types that must extend another class: declare the class final, keep every field private final, provide no setters, copy mutable arguments before validating and never return interior mutable state, and express updates as methods that return a new instance. Static factories give named construction and allow instance interning; when the type genuinely must be extensible, hide a package-private implementation behind an interface with a private constructor.
pitfalls: final on a field freezes the reference only: a final List field still accepts add() and java.util.Date still has setters, so copy on the way in and out or use java.time types.
A non-final class can be subclassed with mutable state, which voids the guarantee for callers holding the base type - declare it final or keep the constructor private.
Letting this escape the constructor (registering a listener, storing it in a static field) publishes a partially initialised object to other threads.
